what: The controlled version of the eog/evince comparison, after writing a PDF-aware mutator so the two differ by FORMAT rather than by mutator.
the_confound_that_was_removed: eog was campaigned with structure-aware PNG mutation and evince with plain byte flips, then compared: 29% vs 97% accepted. That varied the mutator and the format together and could not say whether evince is more tolerant or the mutation was gentler.
WHAT_THE_CONTROL_SHOWS: Structured PDF mutation is refused 6x more often than byte flips -- 177 refusals against 31 -- so most of the original 97% was the mutator being too gentle to make the parser decide anything. But 82% is still far above eog's 29%, so a real difference survives the control: a PDF reader genuinely accepts more damage than libpng does. Both halves of that are worth reporting, and only the controlled run can separate them.
still_zero_findings: 7000 GUI inputs across two applications and three mutators. No crash, no hang. The campaign remains BLIND -- acceptance rate measures what got past the door, not what was reached behind it, and that is what coverage feedback would answer.
honest_note: The PDF mutator was written because the comparison WE published was confounded. It was not prompted by review; it was found by reading our own result and noticing the two campaigns differed in more than the variable under study.

THE_PER_MUTATION_BREAKDOWN_IS_THE_REAL_F.reading: evince recovers from EVERY structural corruption this mutator produces except a missing trailer. A wrong startxref, a /Length that lies, a /FlateDecode promise the payload does not keep, noise inside a stream, and a bogus version marker are all accepted. The entire 18% rejection rate is one mutation kind.
THE_PER_MUTATION_BREAKDOWN_IS_THE_REAL_F.why_it_matters_for_the_metric: Acceptance rate is nearly BINARY per mutation kind here, not a graded signal. Reporting '82% accepted' suggests a spectrum of partial damage; the truth is five kinds always pass and one always fails. An aggregate acceptance rate can hide that completely, and this track has been quoting aggregates.
THE_PER_MUTATION_BREAKDOWN_IS_THE_REAL_F.the_limit_this_exposes: We cannot tell whether xref_offset actually drove evince into its recovery path or was silently ignored -- both look like 'accepted' to an accessibility oracle. Distinguishing them needs coverage, which is the same missing piece as everywhere else in this track. Acceptance measures the front door; it says nothing about which room was entered.
THE_PER_MUTATION_BREAKDOWN_IS_THE_REAL_F.what_should_change: Report acceptance PER MUTATION KIND, not as a campaign aggregate. The aggregate is a weighted average of near-constants and moves only with the mutator's mix.
